hook: In rats, degrading an action-outcome link overwrites learning for good, unlike extinction, which recovers.
summary: Rats learned two lever-reward links, then one was degraded by giving its reward without pressing. Responding stayed low after two weeks and after a surprise reward, unlike the recovery seen after extinction. Silencing the lateral orbitofrontal cortex impaired learning of the degradation but not its recall. Results are from rats on one task type.
title: Lateral orbitofrontal cortex enables new learning to overwrite previously acquired information.
